question.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ z-x+2=-1 \\ 2y-2x-4z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/228e4520f4301ac7acb7eef54fad6dcc8ce9bbf43d48124a761978dfcea6423b.svg)
What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ -x+0y+z=-3 \\ -2x+2y-4z=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/80100c3398fa2eac3a07696dd30354c3c971f0650ab32d67a958492ed1cbdeae.svg)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/8f7fdfc0426ad23a34e6d7f2915181a88a63ea74da93b2b6bd718e03f21ba8d2.svg)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/2867d40f70d0e042e522e1bb14ea8af830e42f22a63cc482ba67923c51807312.svg)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/9a4c39673ffd559b35ed9dbf0e465f6a8714c0d9a467178a51e1f6ad79a81445.svg)

Therefore $a=0,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-3.$
